newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan minister says stocks won't plunge over Deng.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan minister says stocks won't plunge over Deng.

text.p: Taiwan's finance minister Paul Chiu said on Thursday he believed Taiwan's stock market would not plunge over the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, state-funded Central News Agency reported.
"The news of Deng's deteriorating health has been circulated for a long time, the day (of his death) is expected," Chiu told the state news agency.
"I believe the stock market will not plunge," Chiu said.
Chiu told the agency that he was "not a bit surprised" by the news of Deng's death.
The government would closely monitor the impact of Deng's death on local financial markets, Chiu added.
China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection, the Xinhua news agency said.
Deng died at 21.08 p.m. (1308 GMT) at the age of 93, Xinhua said. (( -- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815) ))
